overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic marine layer pattern this morning, with dense fog, a high dewpoint of 62.6°F, and light southerly flow keeping overnight temps locked in the low-to-mid 60s. As of 05:45 ET (~2:45 AM PT), the running max sits at just 66.2°F with near-zero 30-minute velocity, suggesting the marine layer is firmly in control and daytime heating will be constrained. Heat alerts in the region are confined to inland desert and valley areas (San Diego deserts up to 115°F, Inland Empire up to 100°F) and are not relevant to the coastal LA observation site.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model spread today: GFS (78.2°F) and ECMWF (77.3°F) run significantly warmer than NBM (71.8°F) and HRRR (75.6°F), with NWS official at ~75°F. The NBM — typically best-calibrated for marine-influenced coastal sites — aligns most closely with the D1_NOW probabilistic output, which concentrates 59.3% of probability mass in the 72–73°F bucket. The warmer GFS/ECMWF guidance likely underestimates marine layer persistence given the current fog and high dewpoints.
max_temp_prediction: Today's daily high for the LA site is most likely to land in the 72–74°F range, with the D1_NOW model's dominant signal at 72–73°F (59.3%) supported by the NBM's 71.8°F guidance and the strong marine layer setup visible in current observations. The NWS official 75°F forecast and warmer GFS/ECMWF output represent an upside tail if fog burns off faster than expected, but the high dewpoint, southerly onshore flow, and sluggish early morning warming trend favor a cooler outcome. Confidence is moderately high for the active even-bucket market's top bucket (72–73°F), with secondary risk to the 74–75°F bucket if afternoon clearing is more aggressive.
